Check with `python -c "import platform; print(platform.machine())"` — if it says `x86_64` on an M-series Mac, that's the problem. - **Symptoms:** repeated `Intel MKL WARNING: ... SSE4.2 ... deprecated` lines, and/or `zsh: segmentation fault run-pycat` right after `Cellpose model not found in cache — downloading now...` (an Intel build of PyTorch crashing under Rosetta). - **Fix:** install the **native Apple Silicon (arm64)** Miniforge (filename contains `arm64`, not `x86_64`) from the [conda-forge download page](https://conda-forge.org/download/), recreate the `pycat-env`, and confirm `python -c "import platform; print(platform.machine())"` says `arm64` before installing. See the expandable note in Step 2 above for details. 3. **Mac: `conda-libmamba-solver` / `libarchive.19.dylib` error** - **Cause:** a Homebrew-installed Miniconda (path like `/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/miniconda/...`) whose bundled solver library broke after a Homebrew update. This is a conda/Homebrew issue, not a PyCAT one. - **Fix:** use **Miniforge** (from the [conda-forge download page](https://conda-forge.org/download/)) instead of Homebrew's Miniconda, and create your `pycat-env` there. You don't have to uninstall the Homebrew conda — just install Miniforge alongside it and use that. 4. **Mac: `llvmlite needs CMake tools to build`** - **Cause:** `pip` couldn't find a prebuilt `llvmlite`/`numba` for your Mac and tried to compile from source, which needs `cmake`. - **Fix:** install them from conda-forge first (prebuilt, no compiler needed): `conda install -c conda-forge llvmlite numba`, then `pip install "pycat-napari[arm-mac]"`. See Step 3 above. 5. **`ERROR: Could not find a version that satisfies the requirement pycat-napari` (every version rejected)** - **Cause:** your Python is neither 3.9 nor 3.12 — usually 3.10/3.11 from a base environment you didn't mean to install into. `pip` filters out every release because none matches your Python version. - **Fix:** confirm your Python with `python --version` (it must be `3.12.x`), and if not, recreate the environment: `conda create -n pycat-env python=3.12` then activate it before installing. 6. **GUI Issues** - Check PyQt5 installation - Update graphics drivers - Verify you're not running the program from jupyter notebook 7. **Analysis Errors** - Confirm input file format - Check memory availability - View traceback in napari or check your terminal for console errors 8. **Performance Issues** - Slow processing or a spinning wheel in Windows/Mac is normal for condensate segmentation - Check the terminal for the progress printouts of the analysis 9. **File Loading Errors (`newbyteorder` / tifffile)** - See [NumPy 2.0 Compatibility](#numpy-20-compatibility) below 10. **TrackMate Integration Errors** - `ImportError: TrackMate bridge requires pyimagej` — install with `pip install "pycat-napari[trackmate]"` - Java not found — install a JDK 11+ (`mamba install openjdk=11` is the most reliable cross-platform option) and confirm it's on `PATH` with `java -version` - Slow or failed first run — the first TrackMate run downloads a full Fiji distribution over the network; this can take several minutes and will fail without internet access, but only needs to happen once (cached afterward) - The embedded Java process cannot be restarted mid-session — if you change Java/Fiji configuration, restart PyCAT entirely rather than retrying within the same session If the above suggestions did not help, you can use the info below to open an issue or contact the maintainers. Modern AIs (ChatGPT, Claude, etc) are very good at troubleshooting installation issues and error messages, and may be your best option for a fast solution to any non-critical issues. --- ### NumPy 2.0 Compatibility PyCAT requires `numpy<2.0` by default. If you see an error like: ``` AttributeError: `newbyteorder` was removed from the ndarray class in NumPy 2.0 ``` this means your environment has NumPy 2.0 installed, which is incompatible with the version of `tifffile` that PyCAT's dependencies require. #### Option A — Use a fresh environment with NumPy 1.x (recommended) This is the simplest fix and the one we recommend for most users: ```bash mamba create -n pycat-env python=3.12 mamba activate pycat-env pip install pycat-napari ``` A fresh environment will install `numpy<2.0` automatically per PyCAT's requirements. #### Option B — Patch tifffile in your existing NumPy 2.0 environment If you specifically need NumPy 2.0 for other packages in the same environment, download [`fix_tifffile.py`](fix_tifffile.py) from the repository root and run it once: ```bash python fix_tifffile.py ``` This patches one line in your installed `tifffile.py` to use the NumPy 2.0-compatible equivalent and saves a backup as `tifffile.py.bak`. You only need to run it once per environment; it survives PyCAT upgrades. **What the script does:** replaces `result = result.newbyteorder()` with `result = result.view(result.dtype.newbyteorder('='))` — the equivalent call that NumPy 2.0 requires. #### Option C — Downgrade NumPy manually ```bash pip install "numpy<2.0" ``` > ⚠️ **Note:** If you have other packages that require NumPy 2.0, Option B (patching tifffile) is preferable to downgrading. ### Getting Help - Search [existing issues](https://github.com/BanerjeeLab-repertoire/pycat-napari/issues) - Open a [new issue](https://github.com/BanerjeeLab-repertoire/pycat-napari/issues/new) - Contact us at [banerjeelab.org](banerjeelab.org) ## Project Status & Roadmap For the current version, see [PyCAT on PyPI](https://pypi.org/project/pycat-napari/) or run `pip show pycat-napari`. ### Recent Updates See [CHANGELOG.md](CHANGELOG.md) for detailed version history. ### Completed (formerly on this roadmap) - ✅ GPU acceleration for rolling-ball background removal and morphological operations (CuPy, `[gpu]` extra) - ✅ 3D / Z-stack support: full 3D condensate segmentation pipeline, built on the validated 2D per-slice algorithms and linked into true 3D objects across Z - ✅ Time-series support: lazy zarr-backed loading, parallelized preprocessing, keyframe Cellpose, drift correction, per-frame spatial metrics - ✅ Multi-dimensional file I/O: nested time-series-with-Z-stack acquisitions and multi-position/multi-scene files (IMS, OME-TIFF, CZI) - ✅ Batch processing: record-and-replay headless batch runner with per-step error isolation - ✅ Expanded analysis methods: spatial metrology, morphological complexity, organizational metrics, MSD/diffusion, C_sat estimation, fusion/coarsening kinetics, Kaplan-Meier survival - ✅ In vitro (cell-free) condensate analysis pipelines, fluorescence and brightfield - ✅ Optional integration with real TrackMate for trajectory linking ### Roadmap - Extended file format support (including migration to BioIO) and integration with native napari IO - ML classifiers and segmentation models trained on annotated data output by PyCAT - Ground-truth benchmarking for tracking and segmentation accuracy - Statistical comparison tooling across experimental conditions/batches - See our full [Roadmap Page](https://pycat-napari.readthedocs.io/en/latest/development/roadmap.html) for more detailed information and wish list ## Acknowledgments This project was developed by Gable Wadsworth and Christian Neureuter in the Condensate Biophysics Lab (Banerjee Lab) at SUNY Buffalo. ### Key Dependencies - [napari](https://napari.org/) - Image visualization - [scikit-image](https://scikit-image.org/) - Image processing - [numpy](https://numpy.org/) - Numerical computing - [pandas](https://pandas.pydata.org/) - Data analysis - [Cellpose](https://www.cellpose.org/) - Deep-learning cell/nucleus segmentation - [PyTorch](https://pytorch.org/) - Deep learning backend - [BioIO](https://github.com/bioio-devs/bioio) (successor to AICSImageIO) - Microscope file format reading - [zarr](https://zarr.dev/) - Lazy, chunked array storage for large multi-dimensional acquisitions - [scipy](https://scipy.org/) - Scientific computing (optimization, linear assignment, filtering) - Optional: [CuPy](https://cupy.dev/) (GPU acceleration), [StarDist](https://github.com/stardist/stardist) (alternative segmentation), [pyimagej](https://github.com/imagej/pyimagej) (TrackMate bridge) ### Special Thanks - Banerjee Lab members for testing and feedback - napari community for viewer framework - Open source community for supporting libraries For additional details, troubleshooting, and advanced features, see our [full documentation](https://pycat-napari.readthedocs.io/en/latest/).

one_liner: 该仓库提供粗粒化Langevin动力学模拟与LAMMPS输入文件，研究细胞内支架蛋白的相分离（LLPS）对受体聚集的影响，直接面向相分离/凝聚体建模，属于本课题核心方向。

## 是什么

该仓库是论文 *"Phase Separation of Intracellular Proteins Influences Extracellular Signaling at the Synapse"* 的配套代码与数据仓库，由印度理工学院印多尔分校化学工程系的研究者维护。仓库提供了一套粗粒化 Langevin 动力学模拟（基于 LAMMPS）及分析代码，用于研究细胞内支架蛋白的液-液相分离（LLPS）如何影响突触处受体聚集。

仓库包含两个自洽的模拟体系：
- **case1_single_polymer_single_receptor**：单一支架聚合物（Kremer-Grest 珠簧链，N=25）与单一受体物种，比较聚合物在纯排斥（WCA）与吸引（LJ）势下的相行为差异。
- **case2_two_polymer_two_receptor**：两种支架聚合物（P1、P2）与两种受体（R1、R2），通过调节聚合物间相互作用强度（ε(P1-P2)）实现从完全分离的凝聚体到共相分离的拓扑转变。

每个体系包含初始构型构建、生产模拟（LAMMPS 输入文件）和聚类分析脚本。

## 亮点

- **聚焦 LLPS 与受体聚集的耦合**：模型将支架聚合物的相分离行为与膜上受体聚集直接关联，揭示了凝聚态支架可降低受体聚集的临界浓度约 70%，并产生更大的受体簇。
- **双聚合物竞争体系**：case2 系统展示了两种支架聚合物在共相分离时反而抑制受体聚集，说明支架-支架相互作用可拮抗受体聚集，提供了多组分相分离调控信号的新视角。
- **完整的可复现流程**：仓库包含从初始构型（`Input_file.ipynb`）到生产模拟（`lammps_sim.in`）再到聚类分析（`*_cluster_lammps.py`）的完整脚本，并提供了 `run_*.sh` 和 `copy_*.sh` 辅助脚本，便于批量部署和运行。
- **清晰的参数化设计**：通过调节 LJ 势的 ε 值（0.5 为吸引，0.1-0.5 为聚合物间强度）和受体数量（R=0-300），系统性地扫描相分离与聚集行为。

## 为何对本课题有用

本仓库直接面向 LLPS/凝聚体建模，属于课题核心范畴。其价值在于：
- **提供 LLPS 粗粒化模拟的完整范例**：展示了如何用 Kremer-Grest 链和 LJ/WCA 势构建可相分离的支架聚合物，并耦合膜受体，是 IDR/无序蛋白相分离模拟的典型方法。
- **多组分相分离拓扑分析**：case2 中通过改变聚合物间相互作用实现不同凝聚体拓扑（分离、接触、共相分离），并分析其对受体聚集的影响，为研究多组分凝聚体的功能后果提供了可复用的分析框架。
- **聚类分析工具**：仓库中的 `*_cluster_lammps.py` 脚本可计算最大簇分数、簇大小分布等，这些工具可直接迁移到其他 LLPS 模拟数据的分析中。
- **可复现的模拟设置**：LAMMPS 输入文件提供了详细的力场参数（FENE、LJ、WCA），可作为构建类似相分离模型的参考。

## 怎么用

仓库结构清晰，使用步骤如下：

1. **选择体系**：根据研究问题进入 `case1_single_polymer_single_receptor/` 或 `case2_two_polymer_two_receptor/`。
2. **构建初始构型**：运行 `initial_configuration/Input_file.ipynb` 生成起始聚合物构型，并执行 `lammps_sim.in` 进行平衡。
3. **运行生产模拟**：在 `simulations/<condition>/N_<R>/` 目录下，使用 LAMMPS 运行 `lammps_sim.in`（例如 `lmp -in lammps_sim.in`），生成轨迹文件。
4. **分析聚类**：使用 `analysis/` 下的脚本（如 `a_cluster_lammps.py`）计算簇统计量，并通过 `run_*.sh` 批量执行。
5. **汇总结果**：运行 `analysis/fraction_vs_N.py` 和 `analysis/largest_cluster_analysis.py` 等脚本，生成受体/聚合物最大簇分数随受体数量的变化图，复现论文中的 Fig. 3 和 Fig. 5。

注意：原始轨迹文件因体积过大未纳入版本控制，但所有输入文件和脚本均已提供，可完全复现模拟。每个 case 目录下的 `README.md` 提供了更详细的脚本用法说明。
readme:
# Phase Separation of Intracellular Proteins Influences Synaptic Bistability

This repository contains the coarse-grained Langevin dynamics simulations, LAMMPS
input files, and analysis code used in:

> V. Saxena\*, A. A. Totade\*, V. Pandey, G. Chauhan, *"Phase Separation of
> Intracellular Proteins Influences Extracellular Signaling at the Synapse"*
> (\*equal contribution), Department of Chemical Engineering, Indian Institute
> of Technology Indore. Corresponding author: gaurav@iiti.ac.in

## Scientific objective

Neuronal signaling depends on receptor clustering at the plasma membrane, a
process influenced by intracellular scaffold proteins that can themselves
undergo liquid–liquid phase separation (LLPS) into membraneless condensates.
This project asks two questions with a minimal coarse-grained model:

1. **How does receptor clustering at the membrane depend on the phase
   behaviour (dispersed vs. condensed) of a bulk scaffold polymer that binds
   the receptors?**
2. **When two competing scaffold polymers are present, how does their
   relative spatial organization (separate condensates, touching
   condensates, or a single co-phase-separated condensate) modulate
   receptor clustering?**

The model couples a bead-spring (Kremer–Grest) scaffold polymer in a bulk
compartment to monomeric receptor beads confined to an adjacent membrane
compartment, connected through attractive polymer–receptor interactions
across a repulsive wall. See the paper (Sections I–III) for the full
scientific motivation, results, and discussion.

## Repository structure

The two simulation systems described in the paper are kept in separate,
self-contained folders:

```
SIGNALLING-PAPER/
├── case1_single_polymer_single_receptor/   # Section II.A/II.B & Fig. 2–3
└── case2_two_polymer_two_receptor/         # Section II.C & Fig. 4–5
```

Each case folder follows the same internal layout:

```
caseN_.../
├── README.md                  # case-specific methodology and file guide
├── initial_configuration/     # equilibration stage: builds the starting polymer configuration
├── simulations/                # production LAMMPS runs, organized by physical condition, then by receptor count (N_<R>)
├── analysis/                   # analysis scripts, notebooks, and results
```

See `case1_single_polymer_single_receptor/README.md` and
`case2_two_polymer_two_receptor/README.md` for the full breakdown of
conditions, receptor counts, and scripts in each case.

## The two simulation systems

### Case 1 — single scaffold polymer + single receptor species (Section II.A–B)

One scaffold polymer (Kremer–Grest bead-spring chain, N = 25 monomers) in a
bulk compartment, and a single receptor species (monomeric beads) confined to
an adjacent membrane compartment. Two scaffold-polymer interaction models are
compared at receptor counts R = 0, 1, 20, 50, 100, 125, 150, 200, 250, 300:

| Condition | Polymer (P–P) potential | Behaviour |
|---|---|---|
| `WCA_no_phase_separation` | purely repulsive WCA (cutoff 2¹ᐟ⁶σ) | scaffold does **not** phase separate |
| `LJ_eps0.5_phase_separation` | attractive LJ, ε = 0.5 kBT (cutoff 2.5σ) | scaffold **condenses** into a dense phase |

This corresponds to Fig. 2 and Fig. 3 of the paper: condensation of the
scaffold polymer lowers the critical receptor concentration for clustering by
~70% and produces larger receptor clusters at saturation.

### Case 2 — two scaffold polymers + two receptor species (Section II.C, Results III.B)

Two scaffold polymers (P1, P2), each with strong self-attraction
(P1–P1, P2–P2, ε = 0.5), and two receptor species (R1, R2) that each bind
strongly to only one of the two polymers (R1↔P1, R2↔P2). The inter-polymer
interaction strength ε(P1–P2) is varied to change how the two condensed
phases are spatially organized, at receptor counts R1 = R2 = 50, 100, 204:

| Condition (`simulations/cutoff2.5_standard_LJ/`) | ε(P1–P2) | Topology |
|---|---|---|
| `eps0.10_distinct_condensates` | 0.10 | two fully phase-separated condensates |
| `eps0.25_distinct_condensates` | 0.25 | two fully phase-separated condensates |
| `eps0.40_touching_condensates` | 0.40 | condensates just touching |
| `eps0.50_co_phase_separated`   | 0.50 | single co-phase-separated condensate |

This corresponds to Fig. 4 and Fig. 5 of the paper: co-phase separation of
the two polymers (ε = 0.5) *suppresses* receptor clustering relative to
distinct condensates, indicating that competing scaffold–scaffold
interactions can antagonize receptor clustering.

`case2_two_polymer_two_receptor/exploratory/` holds two additional sets of
runs that are **not** among the four published P1–P2 cases above: a
WCA-based (non-attractive) inter-polymer interaction control, and a set of
"core–shell" topology trial runs. Both are preserved for completeness but
are explicitly skipped by the paper's own analysis scripts (see the comment
in `analysis/rdf_e_basecase.py`).

## LAMMPS methodology (summary; see paper Sec. II for full detail)

- Implicit-solvent **Langevin dynamics**, integrated with the velocity-Verlet
  algorithm, damping parameter 1/τ, timestep 0.005τ, in reduced
  Lennard-Jones units.
- Scaffold polymers: Kremer–Grest bead-spring chains, N = 25 monomers per
  chain, bonded via a FENE potential (K = 10, R₀ = 1.0) and non-bonded via a
  Lennard-Jones potential (Eq. 1 in the paper), or a WCA potential (cutoff
  2¹ᐟ⁶σ) for the non-phase-separating control.
  See Table I of the paper for the full non-bonded parameter set (ε, σ,
  cutoff) between every pair of particle types (P1, P2, R1, R2).
- The simulation box is split by a repulsive WCA wall along z into a lower
  (scaffold-polymer) and upper (receptor) compartment, confining receptors
  to the membrane-proximal region and preventing polymers from crossing
  into it.
- Simulations were run with **LAMMPS** (23 Jun 2022 build) in the NVT
  ensemble for 2×10⁷ production steps; the last 200 equilibrated trajectory
  frames were used to compute cluster statistics. Trajectories were
  visualized with **OVITO**.

## Analysis workflow

1. **Initial configuration** (`initial_configuration/`): builds/equilibrates
   the starting scaffold-polymer configuration (`Input_file.ipynb` +
   `lammps_sim.in`), producing the restart file that the production runs
   read from.
2. **Production runs** (`simulations/<condition>/N_<R>/`): each folder holds
   the LAMMPS input script (`lammps_sim.in`) for that specific
   condition/receptor-count combination, plus its own equilibration log
   (`log.polymer_wall.txt`) and, once run, the (large, not version
   controlled) raw trajectory.
3. **Cluster analysis** (`analysis/`): standalone CLI tools
   (`a/b/[c/d]_cluster_lammps.py`, `cluster_lammps.py`,
   `receptor_cluster_lammps.py`) compute connected-component cluster
   statistics from a run's `lammps.data` + `traj.lammpstrj` files. The
   `copy_*.sh` helper scripts deploy these tools (and companion notebooks)
   into every `N_*` folder; the `run_*.sh` scripts then execute them.
4. **Aggregation** (`analysis/fraction_vs_N.py`,
   `analysis/largest_cluster_analysis.py`, `analysis/rdf*.py`,
   `analysis/collect_cluster_plots.py` [case 2 only]): walk every
   condition/receptor-count folder, compute the ensemble-averaged fraction
   of receptors/polymers in the largest cluster as a function of receptor
   count, and produce the summary plots analogous to Fig. 3 and Fig. 5 of
   the paper. Outputs land in `analysis/results/`.

See each case's own `README.md` for the exact command-line usage of every
script.

## Reproducing a simulation

```bash
cd case1_single_polymer_single_receptor/simulations/WCA_no_phase_separation/N_100
lmp -in lammps_sim.in          # requires a local LAMMPS build
```

Raw trajectories (`lammps.data`, `traj.lammpstrj`, restart checkpoints, and
`data*.xyz` OVITO-visualization snapshots) are regenerated by the run and are
**not** version-controlled (see `.gitignore`) because of their size. What is
version-controlled is everything needed to regenerate them: the LAMMPS input
scripts, the shared starting configuration, and the small numeric/plot
results already computed from past runs.


elsewhere; running it against this already-cleaned repository is a no-op
(all source paths will already have been moved).

one_liner: 该仓库提供从结构预测输出中计算局部互作分数(LIS/iLIS)的工具,专门用于识别涉及SLiMs或IDR的瞬时/柔性蛋白互作,与IDR介导的结合建模高度相关,但主要面向PPI发现而非IDR本身。

## 是什么

AFM-LIS 是一个用于从结构预测输出中计算 **Local Interaction Score (LIS)** 的工具仓库，旨在增强蛋白质-蛋白质相互作用 (PPI) 的发现。它特别针对全局置信度指标（如 ipTM）容易遗漏的**瞬时和柔性相互作用**（例如涉及 SLiMs 或 IDR 的相互作用）而设计。仓库支持 AlphaFold3、ColabFold/AlphaFold-Multimer、Boltz、Chai-1 和 OpenFold3 等平台。

## 亮点

- **双框架支持**：提供两种经过验证的分析方法——**iLIS**（集成 LIS，推荐）和原始的 **LIS + LIA** 双指标系统。
- **iLIS 核心机制**：通过几何平均 `iLIS = sqrt(LIS * cLIS)` 结合界面置信度与直接物理接触过滤，有效消除“高置信但无物理接触”的假阳性。
- **命令行工具 `lis.py`**：支持批量分析、自动平台检测、并行处理、增量 CSV 输出，可处理压缩文件。
- **Web 可视化工具 LIVIA**：无需安装，拖拽文件即可在浏览器中查看 PAE/LIS/cLIS 图谱，并生成 ChimeraX/PyMOL 脚本，数据本地处理。
- **批量可视化脚本 `lis_to_cxc.py`**：从 CSV 直接生成 ChimeraX 脚本，便于大规模筛选和图形生成。
- **阈值明确**：提供 iLIS ≥ 0.223 的高置信相互作用建议阈值，以及 LIS + LIA 框架的判定条件。

## 为何对本课题有用

本课题关注 IDR/无序蛋白及其相分离与凝聚体。AFM-LIS 专门针对**柔性相互作用**（如涉及 IDR 的相互作用）进行优化，因为全局指标（如 ipTM）常因无序区域“稀释”而失效。该工具能够从结构预测中识别 IDR 介导的瞬时结合，为研究无序蛋白的互作网络提供计算支持。此外，其输出包含每个链的 LIR（Local Interaction Residues）索引和 pLDDT 信息，可用于分析 IDR 区域的结合位点。

## 怎么用

1. **安装依赖**：确保 Python ≥ 3.8，并安装 NumPy 和 SciPy。
2. **运行 `lis.py`**：
   ```bash
   python lis.py /path/to/prediction_folder/   # 自动检测平台，处理所有模型
   python lis.py alphafold3_output.zip         # 处理 zip 文件
   python lis.py /path/to/predictions/ -w 4    # 并行处理
   ```
3. **自定义布局**：若自动检测失败，可在预测文件夹中放置 `lis.json` 清单文件，指定结构、PAE 和摘要文件的 glob 模式。
4. **可视化**：使用 LIVIA 网页工具进行交互式分析，或运行 `lis_to_cxc.py` 生成 ChimeraX 脚本：
   ```bash
   python lis_to_cxc.py --csv results_lis_analysis.csv --pdb-root . --out cxc/
   ```
5. **解释结果**：根据输出 CSV 中的 iLIS 值（≥ 0.223 为高置信）或 LIS + LIA 阈值判断相互作用。

更多细节和示例请参考仓库 README 和论文。
readme: # AFM-LIS: Local Interaction Score for Structure Predictions This repository provides tools to calculate the Local Interaction Score (LIS) from structure prediction outputs for enhanced protein-protein interaction (PPI) discovery. The LIS framework accurately identifies transient and flexible interactions (e.g., involving SLiMs or IDRs) that global confidence metrics like ipTM often miss. **Supports:** AlphaFold3, ColabFold/AlphaFold-Multimer, Boltz, Chai-1, OpenFold3 The framework includes two validated approaches: - **iLIS (integrated Local Interaction Score)**: Our newest, robust **single metric** that combines interface confidence with a direct physical contact filter. This is the recommended score for most analyses. ([Kim et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.14.718529)) - **LIS + LIA (Local Interaction Score + Area)**: Our original dual-metric system that evaluates interactions by assessing both the _score_ (LIS) and the _area_ (LIA) of the predicted interface. ([Kim et al., 2024](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.02.19.580970v1)) ## How iLIS Works: The Core Concept The iLIS framework identifies the high-confidence local interface, filters it for direct physical contacts, and combines these scores into a single, robust metric. **Schematic of the iLIS calculation and benchmark data**. > **Figure 1** from [Kim et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.14.718529). **(A)** iLIS calculation scheme: the Local Interaction Area (LIA) Map is filtered by direct contacts (cLIA Map), and LIS and cLIS are combined as iLIS = √(LIS × cLIS). **(B–I)** iLIS effectively identifies positive interactions across multiple *Drosophila* PPI datasets (FlyBI Y2H, DPiM AP-MS, DPiM2 AP-MS, Literature), and is particularly informative for flexible protein complexes (low pLDDT groups). ## The Evolution from LIS to iLIS ### 1. The Original Framework: LIS + LIA ### Standard AlphaFold metrics (like ipTM) often fail on flexible interactions because non-interacting disordered regions can "dilute" the global score. Our original **Local Interaction Score (LIS)** was developed to solve this by focusing only on the confidently predicted interface, defined as all residue pairs with a Predicted Aligned Error (PAE) **≤ 12 Å**. However, `LIS` _by itself_ had a potential failure mode: it could assign a high score to a few residue pairs that were confidently predicted but physically distant and not in actual contact. Our original (2024) framework addressed this by using `LIS` in combination with a second metric, the **Local Interaction Area (LIA)**, which measures the area in the confident interface (PAE ≤ 12 Å). In the failure case, the `LIA` score would be tiny, successfully filtering out the false positive. This dual-metric `LIS + LIA system` remains a valid approach. > **Examples of positive PPIs with flexible regions (decent LIS & LIA & low ipTM).** All PPI examples were _experimentally_ proven previously. ### 2. The New Metric: iLIS (integrated LIS) ### The new **iLIS** metric streamlines this process into a single, more robust score. It was designed to solve the same problem by directly integrating a physical contact filter. iLIS is calculated as the geometric mean of two components: - **LIS (Local Interaction Score)**: The same as the original metric; measures the average confidence of the broad LIA (PAE ≤ 12 Å). - **cLIS (contact-filtered LIS)**: A stricter metric that measures the average confidence only for residue pairs that are in direct physical contact (PAE ≤ 12 Å **AND** Cβ–Cβ distance ≤ 8 Å). The final score is: `iLIS = sqrt(LIS * cLIS)` This use of a geometric mean is critical. If no direct physical contacts are confidently predicted (`cLIS = 0`), the final `iLIS` score is forced to zero, robustly eliminating this class of false positives. It now allows single metrics to distinguish positive and negative predictions. > **Examples of positive PPIs with flexible regions (decent iLIS & low ipTM).** All PPI examples were _experimentally_ proven previously. ## Interpreting Results & Thresholds We provide two validated frameworks for analysis. **iLIS is the recommended single-metric approach**. ### 1. Recommended: iLIS Framework (Kim et al., 2026) ### A high-confidence interaction is suggested if: - **iLIS ≥ 0.223** This threshold was established using large-scale Y2H reference sets used in yeast (Yu et al., 2008), fly (Tang et al., 2023), and human (Braun et al., 2009). Please see the details in [Kim et al., 2026](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.14.718529). ### 2. Original: LIS + LIA Framework (Kim et al., 2024) ### A positive PPI is suggested if either of the following conditions is met: - **Best LIS** ≥ 0.203 **AND** **Best LIA** ≥ 3432, or - **Average LIS** ≥ 0.073 **AND** **Average LIA** ≥ 1610. These cutoffs were derived from specific fly (Tang et al., 2023) and human (Braun et al., 2009) reference sets. As always, optimal thresholds may vary by dataset, and experimental validation is highly recommended. ## Usage ### Command-Line Tool: `lis.py` (Recommended for batch analysis) A Python script for calculating LIS metrics from structure prediction outputs. ```bash # Basic usage — auto-detects platform, processes all models python lis.py /path/to/prediction_folder/ # Process a zip file python lis.py alphafold3_output.zip # Parallel processing with 4 CPUs python lis.py /path/to/predictions/ -w 4 # Custom output location python lis.py /path/to/predictions/ -d /path/to/output/ # Show error details for failed predictions python lis.py /path/to/predictions/ -v # Reprocess all (ignore existing results) python lis.py /path/to/predictions/ --no-skip-existing ``` **Features:** - Auto-detects prediction platform from filenames - Handles `.gz` and `.xz` compressed files transparently - Incremental CSV output — safe to interrupt and resume - Progress bar with elapsed time and ETA - Parallel processing with `--workers` - Output sorted by name and rank **Supported platforms (auto-detected):** AlphaFold3 (including the official *local* output and the AF3 Server layout), ColabFold, Boltz-1/2, Chai-1, OpenFold3. **Unrecognized layout? Declare it with a manifest.** For anything auto-detection can't place, drop a `lis.json` in the prediction folder (or pass `--manifest path/to/lis.json`) describing your data. Globs match on filenames **relative to that folder**. All fields optional: - `structure` / `pae` / `summary` — filename globs for the structure, PAE, and scores files - `pae_key` — the JSON key holding the PAE matrix (when it isn't a standard one) - `platform` — force a specific finder (same as `--platform`) - `models` — an explicit `[{name, structure, pae, summary}]` list, for full control Glob mode — one structure/PAE pair per matched structure: ```json {"structure": "*_model.cif", "pae": "*_confidences.json", "pae_key": "pae"} ``` Explicit `models` mode — name each model's files (irregular naming, mixed sub-directories, higher-order complexes): ```json { "models": [ {"name": "runA", "structure": "runA/ranked_0.pdb", "pae": "runA/pae.json", "pae_key": "pae"}, {"name": "runB", "structure": "runB/model.cif", "pae": "runB/pae.npy"} ] } ``` The manifest is checked before auto-detection; with `models` or `pae` it drives parsing directly, with only `platform` it just forces the finder. When a folder has no readable PAE, the error message points here. **Raw AlphaFold2 / AlphaFold-Multimer `.pkl`?** The PAE inside a `result_*.pkl` can be read, but only when you declare it **and** pass `--allow-pickle`: ```json {"structure": "*.pdb", "pae": "result_*.pkl", "pae_key": "predicted_aligned_error"} ``` It is off by default because unpickling executes arbitrary code — only enable it for files you trust (`pae_key` defaults to `predicted_aligned_error`). In most pipelines the same PAE is already written as JSON right next to the pickle, which needs no flag. ### Web Tool: LIVIA For visual analysis with no installation required: - **[LIVIA](https://flyark.github.io/LIVIA/)** (**L**ocal **I**nteraction **VI**sualization and **A**nalysis) — drag & drop prediction files, view PAE/LIS/cLIS maps, generate ChimeraX/PyMOL scripts - Supports all platforms listed above - All analysis runs locally in your browser — no data leaves your device - [Step-by-step tutorial](https://flyark.github.io/LIVIA/tutorials.html) · [GitHub](https://github.com/flyark/LIVIA) ### Batch Visualization: `lis_to_cxc.py` (ChimeraX scripts from `lis.py` output) For large screens, generate per-fold ChimeraX `.cxc` scripts directly from a `lis.py` CSV — no web tool needed. ```bash # 1. Score a prediction python lis.py prediction.zip -o results_lis_analysis.csv # 2. Generate ChimeraX visualizations python lis_to_cxc.py \ --csv results_lis_analysis.csv \ --pdb-root . \ --out cxc/ # 3. Open any cxc in ChimeraX (double-click) ``` Each `.cxc` opens the predicted structure in ChimeraX with: - **LIR** residues colored in a light shade (per-chain palette) - **cLIR** residues colored in the full shade - A 2D label panel showing iLIS, cLIS, ranks, and LIR residues per chain (aggregated boundary) Common flags: `--ilis-cutoff` (default `0.223`), `--top-n`, `--pairs A,B`, `--pairs-file`, `--metadata`, `--plddt`, `--palette`. Full help: `python lis_to_cxc.py --help`. **Tip — figure generation for papers/slides.** After opening a `.cxc` in ChimeraX and orienting the view, save a transparent-background PNG with: ``` save myfigure.png transparentBackground true ``` The same command is included as a commented suggestion at the bottom of every emitted `.cxc` file. ## Output CSV Columns | Column | Description | |--------|-------------| | name | Prediction name | | rank | Rank number | | model | Model number | | iLIS | integrated LIS = √(LIS × cLIS) | | iLIA | integrated LIA = √(LIA × cLIA) | | iLISA | iLIS × iLIA | | ipSAE | interaction prediction Score from Aligned Errors ([Dunbrack, 2025](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2025.02.10.637595)) | | LIS | Local Interaction Score (PAE ≤ 12Å) | | cLIS | contact-filtered LIS (PAE ≤ 12Å & Cβ ≤ 8Å) | | LIA | Local Interaction Area (count of confident residue pairs) | | cLIA | contact-filtered LIA | | ipTM | interface predicted TM-score ([Evans et al., 2021](https://doi.org/10.1101/2021.10.04.463034)) | | pLDDT_i/j | per-chain average pLDDT | | pTM | predicted TM-score | | LIR_i/j | count of Local Interaction Residues per chain | | cLIR_i/j | count of contact-filtered LIR per chain | | LIpLDDT_i/j | average pLDDT of LIR residues per chain | | cLIpLDDT_i/j | average pLDDT of cLIR residues per chain | | len_i/j | chain lengths | | LIR_indices_i/j | LIR residue positions (compact range format) | | cLIR_indices_i/j | cLIR residue positions (compact range format) | | structure_file | source structure filename | ## Requirements For `lis.py`: - Python ≥ 3.8 - NumPy - SciPy ## How to Cite If you use this work, please cite the relevant paper: - **For the iLIS metric (Recommended)**: Kim et al (2026). FlyPredictome: a structural atlas of predicted protein-protein interactions in _Drosophila_. _bioRxiv_ ([link](https://doi.org/10.64898/2026.04.14.718529)) - **For the original LIS + LIA framework**: Kim et al (2024). Enhanced Protein-Protein Interaction Discovery via AlphaFold-Multimer. _bioRxiv_ ([link](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.1101/2024.02.19.580970v1)) ## FlyPredictome Large-scale AlphaFold-Multimer PPI predictions in *Drosophila*, scored with the LIS framework: - **[www.flyrnai.org/tools/fly_predictome/web/](https://www.flyrnai.org/tools/fly_predictome/web/)** - Now covers **>1.5 million** PPI predictions. ## Declaration of Generative AI Usage This project utilized OpenAI's ChatGPT, Google's Gemini, and Anthropic's Claude to assist in generating Python code, documentation, or other textual content.

## 是什么

CELL-FM 是一个虚拟显微镜生成模型，由 Bo Huang 实验室开发。它从蛋白质的氨基酸序列和细胞上下文（如细胞核、微管、内质网等）生成该蛋白质在细胞中应有的荧光图像；反过来，也能从图像生成与之相符的蛋白质序列。该模型基于论文《Virtual experiments bridge sequence and microscopy with generative models》（bioRxiv, doi:10.64898/2026.09.13.751243）。

## 亮点

- **生成式虚拟实验**：不将实验压缩为任务特定的标签，而是直接生成实验读数（蛋白质在细胞中的图像），下游分析（如核质比、凝聚体分类、图像嵌入）可在生成图像上复用真实实验的分析流程，无需针对每个任务重新训练。
- **统一编码器与多任务头**：共享编码器融合图像 token 和序列 token（序列用 ESM-C 600M 蛋白语言模型嵌入），三个输出头分别负责图像生成（MMDiT，流匹配）、序列生成（离散扩散）和图像重建（掩码自编码器，辅助）。
- **两阶段训练**：第一阶段掩码一半图像 patch 以学习稳健共享表征，第二阶段关闭掩码并微调两个生成损失以提升保真度。
- **表达水平条件化**：对于 CondenSeq 数据，表达水平作为额外连续条件 token，使同一序列可在任意浓度下成像，支持虚拟滴定。
- **多数据集训练**：使用 Human Protein Atlas（HPA）、OpenCell 和 CondenSeq 数据集，覆盖固定细胞免疫荧光、活细胞内源标记蛋白以及无序肽段池筛选。
- **应用笔记本**：提供四个 Colab 笔记本，涵盖凝聚体滴定、NLS 筛选、定位信号生成和 OpenCell 虚拟染色，开箱即用。

## 为何对本课题有用

本课题关注固有无序区/无序蛋白（IDR/IDP）及其相分离与生物分子凝聚体（LLPS/condensates）。CELL-FM 直接针对这一方向：

- **凝聚体形成预测**：CondenSeq 数据集包含 14,598 个 66 氨基酸的无序肽段，在 U2AS 细胞核中表达，CELL-FM 可生成这些肽段在不同表达水平下的荧光图像，并用 ViT 分类器判断凝聚或弥散状态，输出滴定曲线（AUC 和 AAC 指标），直接用于研究 IDR 的相分离倾向和再入溶解行为。
- **序列-表型映射**：模型从序列生成图像，使研究者能够通过虚拟实验观察 IDR 序列变异对凝聚体形成的影响，无需湿实验。
- **定位信号设计**：从图像到序列的生成能力可用于设计核定位信号（NLS）或核输出信号（NES），这些信号常与 IDR 功能相关。
- **虚拟染色**：可将任意蛋白质（包括 IDR 蛋白）虚拟染色到细胞中，用于定位和凝聚体分析。

因此，CELL-FM 为 IDR/相分离研究提供了生成式虚拟实验工具，尤其适合高通量筛选和机制探索。

## 怎么用

- **环境**：推荐使用 Colab GPU（T4 即可），笔记本会自动安装依赖并下载权重。
- **应用笔记本**：
  - `notebooks/condensate_titration.ipynb`：对 66 氨基酸无序肽段进行表达水平梯度成像，调用凝聚/弥散分类器，生成滴定曲线并计算 AUC 和 AAC。
  - `notebooks/nls_screening.ipynb`：沿蛋白质序列滑动窗口，虚拟染色每个片段，计算核质比以定位 NLS。
  - `notebooks/pls_generation.ipynb`：从图像生成序列，设计 NLS/NES 肽段，并与人类蛋白质组比较残基组成。
  - `notebooks/opencell_vs.ipynb`：将 OpenCell 蛋白虚拟染色到同一细胞核，用 ViT 嵌入映射蛋白定位。
- **代码结构**：
  - `cell_fm/`：模型（CELL-FM、VAE、ViT 分类器）、数据集、训练流程和任务。
  - `scripts/`：训练和评估的启动脚本。
  - `notebooks/`：应用笔记本。
- **权重**：从 Hugging Face（BoHuangLab/CELL-FM）下载。
- **依赖**：笔记本的依赖版本固定说明见 `notebooks/README.md`。
- **许可证**：MIT。

# CELL-FM

**CELL-FM** is a virtual microscopy model. From a protein's amino-acid sequence and a cellular
context, it generates the fluorescence image that protein would give; from an image, it
generates sequences consistent with it.

Code for [*Virtual experiments bridge sequence and microscopy with generative models*](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.13.751243v1)
(Dihan Zheng, Kibeom Hong, Bo Huang).

| | |
|---|---|
| Paper | [bioRxiv, doi:10.64898/2026.09.13.751243](https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.13.751243v1) |
| Weights | [huggingface.co/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM](https://huggingface.co/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM) |

## Virtual experiments

Predictive models usually compress an experiment into task-specific labels, such as a
localization class, before learning. CELL-FM instead learns to generate the experimental
readout itself: the image of a protein in a cell. Phenotypes are then measured on generated
images with the same analysis used on real ones — a nucleus-to-cytoplasm ratio, a condensate
classifier, an image embedding. One model serves many downstream questions without retraining,
and its results stay directly comparable to the real assay.

## Method

CELL-FM models images as a continuous distribution and protein sequences as a discrete one,
with a shared encoder and a separate decoder for each output.

**Tokens.** The protein channel and the cell-context channels (the nucleus, plus microtubules and
ER for HPA) are encoded by a VAE and cut into patch tokens. The sequence is embedded with the
ESM-C 600M protein language model.

**Unified encoder.** A single transformer attends over image and sequence tokens together and
fuses them into one shared representation.

**Three heads** read from that representation:

| Head | Objective | Role |
|---|---|---|
| Image generator (MMDiT) | Flow matching in VAE latent space | sequence + cell → protein image |
| Sequence generator | Discrete diffusion (order-agnostic autoregressive) | image + cell → sequence |
| Image reconstruction | Denoising masked autoencoder | auxiliary, stage 1 only |

**Training.** Stage 1 optimizes all three losses with half of the image patches masked, to learn
a robust shared representation. Stage 2 turns masking off and fine-tunes the two generative
losses for fidelity.

**Sampling.** An image is generated by integrating the learned flow from Gaussian noise and
decoding the latent with the VAE. A sequence starts fully masked and is filled in one position
at a time, in random order.

**Expression level.** For CondenSeq, protein expression level is an extra continuous
conditioning token, so the same sequence can be imaged at any concentration. This is what makes
*in silico* titration possible.

### Training data

| Dataset | What it images | Scale | Used for |
|---|---|---|---|
| [Human Protein Atlas](https://virtualcellmodels.cziscience.com/dataset/hpa-subcellular-section) | Immunofluorescence in fixed cells; nucleus, microtubule and ER context | 12,894 proteins, 1.1 M single-cell images | Pretraining, localization, signal design |
| [OpenCell](https://opencell.sf.czbiohub.org/) | Endogenously tagged proteins in live HEK293T; nucleus context | 1,311 proteins, ~96,000 single-cell images | Fine-tuning from HPA for virtual staining |
| [CondenSeq](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/biostudies/bioimages/studies/S-BIAD1738) | Intrinsically disordered peptides in U2OS nuclei, pooled screen; nucleus context | 14,598 peptides of 66 aa, ~8 M single-cell images | Condensate formation across expression levels |

## Applications

Each application is a Colab notebook in [`notebooks/`](notebooks). Choose a GPU runtime (a Colab
T4 works); the notebook installs its own dependencies and downloads the weights on first run.

| Notebook | What it does | |
|---|---|---|
| [Condensate titration](notebooks/condensate_titration.ipynb) | Images a 66-aa intrinsically disordered peptide along a ladder of expression levels, calls each image condensed or diffuse with a ViT classifier, and turns the calls into a titration curve summarised by **AUC** (propensity to condense) and **AAC** (re-entrant dissolution at high concentration). | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM/blob/master/notebooks/condensate_titration.ipynb) |
| [NLS screening](notebooks/nls_screening.ipynb) | Slides a window along a protein sequence, virtually stains a cell with each fragment, and scores the nucleus-to-cytoplasm signal ratio per window to locate nuclear localization signals. | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM/blob/master/notebooks/nls_screening.ipynb) |
| [Localization signal generation](notebooks/pls_generation.ipynb) | Runs the model from image to sequence: shown a cell whose protein sits in the nucleus or in the cytoplasm, it designs NLS or NES peptides, then compares their residue composition with the human proteome. | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM/blob/master/notebooks/pls_generation.ipynb) |
| [OpenCell virtual staining](notebooks/opencell_vs.ipynb) | Paints any OpenCell protein onto the same nucleus from its sequence, then embeds the generated cells with a ViT to map where proteins localize. | [![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/BoHuangLab/CELL-FM/blob/master/notebooks/opencell_vs.ipynb) |

Notes on the notebooks' dependency pins are in [`notebooks/README.md`](notebooks/README.md).

## Repository layout

| Path | Contents |
|---|---|
| [`cell_fm/`](cell_fm) | Models (CELL-FM, VAE, ViT classifiers), datasets, training pipeline and tasks |
| [`scripts/`](scripts) | Launch scripts for training and evaluation |
| [`notebooks/`](notebooks) | Application notebooks |

## Citation

If you use CELL-FM, please cite:

```bibtex
@article{zheng2026virtual,
  title   = {Virtual experiments bridge sequence and microscopy with generative models},
  author  = {Zheng, Dihan and Hong, Kibeom and Huang, Bo},
  journal = {bioRxiv},
  year    = {2026},
  doi     = {10.64898/2026.09.13.751243},
  url     = {https://www.biorxiv.org/content/10.64898/2026.09.13.751243v1}
}
```

[MIT](LICENSE)

## 是什么

这是一个基于 Modal 平台的无服务器（serverless）AlphaFold2-Multimer 结构预测流水线，专门用于建模 Munc13-1 蛋白的大分子复合物和活性区凝聚体（active zone condensates）。仓库通过将全长 Munc13-1（约 5200 残基的三聚体）拆分为三个生物学上合理的构建体（Construct A/B/C），绕过了其内部高度灵活、易聚集的固有无序区（IDR，残基 151–528）带来的计算难题，从而在 GPU 显存限制内获得可处理的原子级结构预测。

## 亮点

- **针对 IDR 的构建体设计**：明确将无序 linker（残基 151–528）排除在预测目标之外，设计了三个构建体：
  - Construct A：Munc13C 三聚体（3×1145 AA），评估直立三聚体 MUN 界面；
  - Construct B：MUN-C2C 最小三聚体（3×569 AA），评估静电接触补丁（K1495/K1500 与 D1358/D1369）；
  - Construct C：活性区凝聚体异二聚体（C2A 150 AA + RIM1α 锌指 120 AA），捕捉突触支架开关。
- **大规模多聚体的内存优化**：使用 80 GB NVIDIA A100 GPU，通过 `TF_FORCE_UNIFIED_MEMORY="0"` 和 `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION="0.90"` 预分配约 73.5 GB 物理显存，彻底消除统一内存分页和 CPU 页错误抖动，避免 gVisor 沙箱死锁。Construct B（1707 残基，3 链）在 3 次 recycle 下 5 分钟内完成折叠。
- **冷启动预防**：将 AlphaFold2 模型权重（约 5 GB）存储在持久化的 `modal.Volume` 中，预下载并提交，避免推理时的多 GB 下载延迟；输出也持久化备份。
- **内置质量检查**：`analyze_results.py` 自动计算关键界面的 PAE 指标（如 Construct B 的静电补丁、Construct A 的 MUN 核心、Construct C 的异二聚体界面），并生成带链边界的注释 PAE 热图。
- **PyMOL 可视化**：提供 `visualize_construct_b.py` 生成高分辨率渲染和交互式会话文件（.pse）。

## 为何对本课题有用

本课题关注 IDR/IDP 及其相分离与凝聚体。该仓库直接针对 Munc13-1 的固有无序区（IDR）进行策略性处理：由于 IDR 导致全长蛋白严重聚集并超出 GPU 显存，仓库通过构建体拆分绕开 IDR，同时保留了对凝聚体相关界面的预测能力（如 Construct C 的活性区凝聚体异二聚体）。这为 IDR 介导的凝聚体结构研究提供了一种实用的计算管线范例，展示了如何在资源受限条件下利用 AlphaFold2-Multimer 预测含 IDR 蛋白的复合物结构，并提供了界面质量评估工具。

## 怎么用

1. **安装依赖**：使用 `uv` 包管理器（`curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh`），然后运行 `uv sync` 自动创建虚拟环境并同步锁定依赖。
2. **验证目标**：本地干跑检查 FASTA 多聚体语法和残基完整性：`uv run python run_prediction.py --all --dry-run`。
3. **预缓存权重**：运行 `uv run python run_prediction.py --download-weights` 提前下载模型权重到持久卷，避免推理延迟。
4. **运行预测**：
   - 单个构建体：`uv run python run_prediction.py --target construct_b`（或 `construct_a`、`construct_c`）
   - 全部构建体：`uv run python run_prediction.py --all`
5. **结果验证**：输出同步到 `outputs/<target_name>/`，包含 PDB 文件、评分 JSON（pLDDT、PAE、pTM、ipTM）和注释 PAE 热图。运行 `uv run python analyze_results.py outputs/construct_b targets/construct_b.fasta` 重新检查界面质量。
6. **可视化**：运行 `uv run visualize_construct_b.py` 生成 PyMOL 渲染和会话文件。

# Serverless Munc13-1 AlphaFold2-Multimer Prediction Pipeline on Modal

A high-performance, serverless structural prediction pipeline built on [Modal](https://modal.com) using `colabfold_batch` (AlphaFold2-multimer v3) to model Munc13-1 macromolecular complexes and active zone condensates.

---

## 1. Biological Context & Target Constructs

Full-length Munc13-1 is a massive homooligomer (~5,200 residues as a trimer) containing an extensive, highly flexible intrinsically disordered linker (residues 151–528) that causes severe aggregation and exceeds GPU VRAM boundaries. To achieve tractable, atomistic structural predictions, the computational targets are divided into three biologically grounded constructs:

| Construct | Name | Subunits / Stoichiometry | Residues per Monomer | Total Residues | Key Interface / Biological Purpose |
| :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **Construct A** | **Munc13C Trimer** | $A_3$ Homotrimer | 1,145 AA | 3,435 AA | Functional core (residues 529–1735, $\Delta$ 1408–1452 replaced with EF) evaluating the upright trimer MUN interface. |
| **Construct B** | **MUN-C2C Minimal Trimer** | $B_3$ Homotrimer | 569 AA | 1,707 AA | Reduced-memory test evaluating the electrostatic trimer contact patch (K1495/K1500 and D1358/D1369). |
| **Construct C** | **Active Zone Condensate Heterodimer** | $C_1 : C_2$ Heterodimer | 150 AA + 120 AA | 270 AA | Munc13-1 C2A (1–150) paired with RIM1α zinc-finger domain (1–120) capturing synaptic scaffolding switch. |

---

## 2. Architecture & Memory Management

### Memory Optimization for Massive Multimers
- **80 GB NVIDIA A100 GPU** (`modal.gpu.A100(size="80GB")` / `"A100-80GB"`).
- **Physical High-Bandwidth VRAM Allocation**: `TF_FORCE_UNIFIED_MEMORY="0"` and `XLA_PYTHON_CLIENT_MEM_FRACTION="0.90"` preallocate ~73.5 GB of native physical VRAM upfront. This completely eliminates unified memory paging, CPU page fault thrashing, and gVisor `cuMemAllocManaged` sandbox syscall deadlocks.
- **Fast Execution**: Construct B (1,707 residues, 3 chains) folds in **under 5 minutes** on the 80 GB A100 with 3 recycles.

### Cold-Start Prevention with Persistent Modal Volumes
- AlphaFold2 model weights (~5 GB) are stored in a dedicated `modal.Volume("colabfold-params")` mounted to `/root/params`.
- Pre-downloading and committing weights ensures weights are cached permanently across executions, eliminating multi-gigabyte download latency during inference.
- An additional `modal.Volume("colabfold-outputs")` persistently backs up all generated predictions in the cloud.

---

## 3. Directory Layout

```text
running-af2/
├── pyproject.toml          # Project configuration, dependencies, and metadata managed by uv
├── uv.lock                 # Deterministic dependency lockfile
├── app.py                  # Modal App, container image (ColabFold, Jax CUDA 12), and persistent volume
├── runner.py               # Remote inference function running colabfold_batch on 80 GB A100
├── run_prediction.py       # Local CLI entrypoint with streaming logs and automatic synchronization
├── analyze_results.py      # PAE heatmap plotting, chain demarcation, and trimer contact quality checks
├── targets/                # Input FASTA files (chains delimited by ':')
│   ├── construct_a.fasta   # Construct A (Munc13C Trimer, 3x 1,145 AA)
│   ├── construct_b.fasta   # Construct B (MUN-C2C Minimal Trimer, 3x 569 AA)
│   └── construct_c.fasta   # Construct C (C2A - RIM1α heterodimer, 150 AA : 120 AA)
├── outputs/                # Local synchronized results (.pdb, .json, .a3m, .png)
└── .venv/                  # Local Python virtual environment managed by uv
```

---

## 4. Quickstart & Usage

### 4.1 Install `uv` & Sync Environment
This repository is managed with [`uv`](https://docs.astral.sh/uv/), an extremely fast Python package manager and project resolver.

```bash
# Install uv (if not already installed)
curl -LsSf https://astral.sh/uv/install.sh | sh

# Automatically create virtual environment (.venv) and sync locked dependencies
uv sync
```

Alternatively, you can activate the virtual environment manually:
```bash
source .venv/bin/activate
```

### 4.2 Validate Targets (Dry Run)
Verify multimer FASTA syntax (`>header\nCHAIN1:CHAIN2:...`) and residue integrity locally without initiating cloud compute:
```bash
uv run python run_prediction.py --all --dry-run
```

### 4.3 Pre-Cache Model Weights
Explicitly trigger parameter download and volume commit to prevent inference latency:
```bash
uv run python run_prediction.py --download-weights
```

### 4.4 Run Predictions
Predict single constructs or all constructs using `uv run`:
```bash
# Run Construct B (Minimal Trimer - reduced memory benchmark)
uv run python run_prediction.py --target construct_b

# Run Construct C (C2A - RIM1α active zone heterodimer)
uv run python run_prediction.py --target construct_c

# Run Construct A (Full Munc13C Trimer, 3,435 residues)
uv run python run_prediction.py --target construct_a

# Run all targets sequentially
uv run python run_prediction.py --all
```

---

## 5. Output Verification & Quality Checks

Upon job completion, files are synchronized to `outputs/<target_name>/`:
- `<target>_relaxed_rank_001_...pdb`: Amber-relaxed top-ranked structure coordinates.
- `<target>_scores_rank_001_...json`: Per-residue pLDDT, predicted aligned error (PAE) matrix, pTM, and ipTM.
- `<target>_pae_annotated.png`: Annotated PAE heatmap with dashed chain boundaries and chain labels.

### Specific Interface Metrics
The built-in analysis tool automatically verifies critical contact interfaces:
- **Construct B Trimer Electrostatic Patch**: Computes minimum and mean PAE between the basic patch (K1495/K1500) of Chain $i$ and the acidic patch (D1358/D1369) of Chain $i+1$.
- **Construct A Trimer MUN Core**: Computes inter-chain PAE across the upright trimer contact face.
- **Construct C Active Zone Heterodimer**: Evaluates the binding interface between Munc13-1 C2A (1–150) and RIM1α zinc finger (1–120).

To re-run quality checks on existing predictions at any time:
```bash
uv run python analyze_results.py outputs/construct_b targets/construct_b.fasta
```

### PyMOL 3D Visual Rendering
To generate high-resolution PyMOL renderings and interactive session files (`.pse`) with automatic script dependency resolution:
```bash
uv run visualize_construct_b.py
```

### Example Structural Validation (Construct B Minimal Trimer)

| Trimer Assembly & Chains | Electrostatic Contact Zoom | Annotated PAE Heatmap |
| :---: | :---: | :---: |
| ![Construct B Chains](assets/construct_b_pymol_chains.png) | ![Contact Patch](assets/construct_b_pymol_contact_zoom.png) | ![Construct B PAE](assets/construct_b_pae_annotated.png) |
| *Construct B* $B_3$ *homotrimer colored by chain* | *Basic patch (K1495/K1500) and acidic patch (D1358/D1369)* | *Inter-chain PAE demarcated with chain boundaries* |

## 是什么

`kakutani_pharma` 是一个面向**固有无序蛋白（IDP）构象系综**的统计药理学分析工具包，当前版本聚焦于通过 Kakutani 二分法（Kakutani Dichotomy）相关指标来研究 tau 和 Aβ42 等无序蛋白单体的淀粉样成核抑制问题。仓库包含 Python 包（`kakutani_pharma/`）、实验脚本（`code/exp10_*.py`）、LaTeX 论文（`paper/paper10_*.tex`）以及结果表格（`results/`）。

核心功能是计算构象系综的 **Kakutani 指数（DKI, CKI）**、**谱指纹（spectral fingerprint）** 和 **壳层标度（shell scaling）**，这些指标源自分子动力学（MD）轨迹，用于量化无序蛋白的构象特征。

## 亮点

- **针对 IDP 的专用分析**：直接面向 tau 和 Aβ42 等固有无序蛋白单体，而非通用分子模拟工具。
- **统计药理学视角**：通过尾指数稳定化（tail-exponent stabilization）、非对称基线三次校正（asymmetric baseline cubic corrections）和有限模式交叉（finite-mode crossover）来建模淀粉样成核的阻断。
- **完整的研究管线**：包含 Python 库、实验脚本、测试（`tests/`）和论文生成脚本（`paper10_compute_tables.py`），可复现论文中的表格。
- **轻量依赖**：仅依赖 NumPy、SciPy、Matplotlib，可选支持 MDTraj 用于轨迹处理。

## 为何对本课题有用

本课题关注 IDR/IDP 的构象系综分析与相分离/凝聚体建模。该仓库提供了从 MD 轨迹计算构象系综定量指标（Kakutani 指数、谱指纹、壳层标度）的工具，这些指标可用于描述 IDP 的构象异质性和稳定性，进而可能关联到相分离倾向或淀粉样聚集的抑制机制。虽然仓库未直接涉及 LLPS 模拟，但其对 IDP 单体构象的统计刻画方法可为本课题中 IDP 构象系综分析提供参考或扩展基础。

## 怎么用

1. **安装**：通过 `pip install .` 安装包，或使用 `pip install -e .[md,test]` 安装可选依赖（MDTraj 和测试工具）。
2. **运行实验**：执行 `python code/exp10_ad_tau_abeta_idp_stabilizer.py` 进行 tau/Aβ42 的稳定化实验。
3. **生成论文表格**：运行 `python code/paper10_compute_tables.py` 生成 `results/` 下的 LaTeX 表格。
4. **测试**：使用 `pytest` 运行 `tests/` 下的测试，验证核心功能。
5. **集成**：可将 `kakutani_pharma` 中的函数（如 `calibration.py`、`estimators.py`、`featurizer.py`、`scaling.py`）用于自定义的 IDP 构象系综分析流程。
readme:
﻿# Statistical Pharmacology via Kakutani Dichotomy X

**Blocking the Amyloid Nucleation Phase Transition of Intrinsically Disordered Proteins: Tau PHF6\*/PHF6, the Aβ42 Monomer, and the Kinetic Ensemble Stabiliser Design Law**

[![DOI](https://zenodo.org/badge/DOI/10.5281/zenodo.23068156.svg)](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23068156)

Zhengyi Chen<sup>1</sup>, Ruqing Chen<sup>2</sup>

<sup>1</sup> Guangxi Key Laboratory of Drug Discovery and Optimization, School of Pharmacy, Guilin Medical University, Guilin 541199, P. R. China — chenzhengyi@glmc.edu.cn
<sup>2</sup> GUT Geoservice Inc., Montreal, Québec, Canada — ruqing@hotmail.com

Paper X of the series applies the α<sub>c</sub> = 1/2 criticality theorem of **Paper I** (DOI [10.5281/zenodo.23018827](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23018827)) to the intrinsically disordered aggregation-prone segments of Alzheimer's disease. Where Papers VII–IX worked with folded proteins and covariance, this one works with an IDP, where there is no fixed pocket to dock into and the only structure is a *distribution over contacts*.

## Status

Experiment 10 is complete and passes all 11 acceptance criteria (`results/exp10_console_log.txt`, runtime about 5 s). The companion script passes its 16 checks (`results/paper10_tables_summary.txt`). The unit tests pass: 17 model tests plus the 12 inherited package tests.

The paper is complete: `paper/paper10_ad_tau_abeta_idp_stabilizer.tex` and `.pdf`, 18 pages, compiling with zero errors, zero warnings and zero overfull or underfull boxes. Its numbers come from `code/paper10_compute_tables.py`, which writes `results/paper10_tables_summary.txt`, the table rows `results/paper10_table{1..9}_rows.tex` and `results/paper10_tables.json`.

DOI: [10.5281/zenodo.23068156](https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.23068156). Repository: [Ruqing1963/kakutani-statistical-pharmacology-X](https://github.com/Ruqing1963/kakutani-statistical-pharmacology-X).

## The idea

The monomer ensemble is a product measure on {coil, β} over contact modes. The healthy soluble ensemble and the pathogenic pre-nucleation ensemble differ by

$$\epsilon_i = p_i^{(\beta)} - p_i^{(\mathrm{coil})},$$

which splits in two:

| part | what it is | depends on α? |
|---|---|---|
| **hot spots** | PHF6\* `VQIINK` and PHF6 `VQIVYK` (tau); the central hydrophobic cluster `KLVFFA` and the C-terminus (Aβ) | no |
| **tail** | *N* = 1000 long-range contact modes, ε<sub>i</sub> = c·i<sup>−α</sup> | yes |

By Paper I, Theorem 3.1 the tail sum converges for α > 1/2 and diverges for α ≤ 1/2. So the two ensembles are **equivalent** above the critical exponent and **mutually singular** below it. Below it a nucleus is a distinct phase and does not dissolve back; above it, it does. Hyperphosphorylation lowers α; the design law of a kinetic ensemble stabiliser is to raise it back.

**The stabiliser acts on α alone.** `K_hot` is identical in every row of every table, so the entire effect is attributable to the tail exponent. That is the claim being tested, and making the hot spots inert is what makes the test honest.

## Main results

### Proposition 2.1 — the expansion away from p = 1/2

Paper I worked at p₀ = 1/2, where the symmetry p → 1−p kills the odd terms and the first correction is quartic. A disordered coil is *not* equally likely to be β, so the application cannot use the symmetric case. Expanding both square roots:

$$h(\epsilon) = \underbrace{\frac{\epsilon^2}{4p_0(1-p_0)}}_{A_1} - \underbrace{\frac{\epsilon^3}{8}\left(\frac{1}{p_0^2}-\frac{1}{(1-p_0)^2}\right)}_{B_1} + O(\epsilon^4).$$

At p₀ = 0.15 this gives A₁ = 1.9608 and B₁ = 5.3825, so the relative error of the quadratic term is 2.745·ε — **measured 2.745×10⁻⁴ at ε = 10⁻⁴**, agreeing with the closed form to 1.7×10⁻⁴. The cubic coefficient is odd about 1/2 and vanishes there exactly, recovering Paper I.

**This matters downstream**: it makes the corrections to Paper I's asymptotic constants O(c) rather than O(c²), which is why Paper I could use c = 0.1 and still match A ln 2 to ten digits while this paper, at the physical c = 0.35, cannot.

### Evaluating h without cancellation

The textbook form `h = 2(1 − √(pq) − √((1−p)(1−q)))` subtracts two numbers of order one to produce a result of order ε². This library uses the exact identity

$$h = (p-q)^2\left[\left(\sqrt{p}+\sqrt{q}\right)^{-2} + \left(\sqrt{1-p}+\sqrt{1-q}\right)^{-2}\right],$$

which has none. Against the series of Proposition 2.1:

| ε | stable form | textbook form | gain |
|---|---|---|---|
| 10⁻³ | 1.18×10⁻⁵ | 1.18×10⁻⁵ | 1× |
| 10⁻⁴ | 1.19×10⁻⁷ | 1.22×10⁻⁷ | 1.03× |
| 10⁻⁵ | 1.19×10⁻⁹ | 5.77×10⁻⁷ | 485× |
| 10⁻⁶ | 1.39×10⁻¹¹ | 4.95×10⁻⁵ | **3.6×10⁶×** |

The stable form keeps falling as ε² (the quartic residual); the textbook form turns round and *grows* once cancellation dominates. `kakutani_pharma.compute_dki` uses the textbook form, which is harmless when two ensembles differ appreciably but not when the tail modes are the object of study.

### The trichotomy, and what the estimator recovers

| α | K(10²) | K(10³) | K(10⁴) | K(10⁵) | Π(10⁵) | slope | 1−2α | α̂ | phase |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 0.25 | 3.275 | 11.97 | 41.44 | 138.8 | 6.7×10⁻³¹ | +0.5188 | +0.5 | 0.2406 | singular |
| 0.30 | 2.489 | 7.464 | 20.80 | 55.54 | 8.5×10⁻¹³ | +0.4152 | +0.4 | 0.2924 | singular |
| 0.50 | 0.952 | 1.476 | 2.019 | 2.569 | 2.8×10⁻¹ | +0.0047 | 0.0 | 0.4977 | singular |
| 0.72 | 0.455 | 0.500 | 0.517 | 0.523 | 7.7×10⁻¹ | −0.4389 | −0.44 | 0.7195 | equivalent |
| 0.85 | 0.342 | 0.352 | 0.355 | 0.355 | 8.3×10⁻¹ | −0.6995 | −0.70 | 0.8498 | equivalent |

The doubling estimator of Paper I recovers α to **0.0094** at the physical c = 0.35 and to **3.4×10⁻⁴** at c = 0.01; the residual bias *is* the cubic term, and it falls as c¹ exactly as Proposition 2.1 predicts.

### The three tau states

| state | α | K_hot | K_tail | K_N | Π_N | phase | ΔG‡ | t½ |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| healthy | 0.85 | 1.2035 | 0.3525 | 1.556 | 4.51×10⁻¹ | equivalent | 26.09 kT | 5.8×10⁸ h |
| critical | 0.50 | 1.2035 | 1.4756 | 2.679 | 2.56×10⁻¹ | singular | 23.27 kT | 3.4×10⁷ h |
| **hyperphosphorylated** | **0.30** | 1.2035 | 7.4637 | 8.667 | 1.27×10⁻² | **singular** | 8.22 kT | **10.0 h** |
| **KMS-Tau-204** | **0.72** | 1.2035 | 0.5000 | 1.704 | 4.18×10⁻¹ | **equivalent** | 25.72 kT | **4.0×10⁸ h** |

The stabiliser moves t½ by a factor **4.0×10⁷**, from under a day to beyond any experimental timescale, by moving α from 0.30 to 0.72 and nothing else.

### The transition is a crossover at finite N

This is the result we want to state carefully, because it is where the model is most easily oversold. α<sub>c</sub> = 1/2 is an **N → ∞** statement. At finite N there is no jump — only a crossover, whose position depends on N:

| N | α at which t½ crosses 100 h |
|---|---|
| 10² | 0.131 |
| 10³ | 0.314 |
| 10⁴ | 0.390 |
| 10⁵ | 0.429 |

The threshold rises monotonically and approaches 1/2 **from below**. A figure showing a sharp step at α = 1/2 for a 1000-mode system would be a fabrication; panel E shows the family of crossovers instead.

### Aβ42 against Aβ40

| peptide | K_hot | K_N | ΔG‡ | t½ |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Aβ42 | 1.0906 | 8.554 | 8.50 kT | 13.3 h |
| Aβ40 | 0.6633 | 8.127 | 9.58 kT | 39.0 h |

Aβ42 nucleates **2.93× faster**, from the two extra C-terminal residues alone — the tail exponent is identical in the two rows. The model therefore *under-predicts* the experimental gap, because Aβ42 also differs from Aβ40 in its long-range contact order, which this comparison holds fixed.

## Limits

- **(a)** Contact modes are an abstraction. There is no structure, no trajectory and no force field here: the ensemble is a product measure, and the index is computed from it exactly.
- **(b)** The hot-spot excesses (ε = 0.26–0.30) and the tail amplitude (c = 0.35) are chosen, not measured. What is *not* chosen is that the stabiliser acts only on α.
- **(c)** The barrier law ΔG‡ = G₀ − λK_N is phenomenological, with λ and G₀ calibrated so that hyperphosphorylated tau has t½ = 10 h at N = 1000. Every other half-time in the paper follows from that one anchor.
- **(d)** `KMS-Tau-204` is a point in the model's parameter space, not a compound. The model says what α_eff a stabiliser must reach; it does not say what molecule reaches it.
- **(e)** Product measures assume the contact modes are independent. Real IDP contacts are not, and correlated modes would change the critical exponent. This is the most consequential simplification in the paper.

## Repository layout

```
.
├── kakutani_pharma/     # package inherited from Papers VII-IX
├── code/
│   ├── exp10_lib.py                          # ensembles, hot spots, index, estimator, kinetics
│   ├── exp10_ad_tau_abeta_idp_stabilizer.py  # the experiment
│   └── paper10_compute_tables.py             # companion: table rows and 16 checks
├── tests/
│   ├── test_exp10.py                         # 17 model tests
│   ├── test_kakutani_pharma.py               # 8 inherited

├── data/                # exp10_scaling.csv, exp10_states.csv, exp10_alpha_scan.csv,

├── figures/             # fig10_ad_tau_abeta_idp_stabilizer.{pdf,png}

├── results/             # exp10_console_log.txt, paper10_tables_summary.txt,
│                        # paper10_table*_rows.tex, paper10_tables.json
├── paper/               # paper10_ad_tau_abeta_idp_stabilizer.tex / .pdf
```

## 是什么

**Lipidation Classifier Predictor** 是一个用于预测三肽（tripeptide）组装行为的机器学习工具。它根据每个残基的 AAindex 理化性质（经 PCA 降维）作为特征，使用三个模型（SVM、弹性网络逻辑回归、随机森林）进行投票，将三肽分类为 `fiber`（纤维）、`droplet`（液滴）或 `MetaStable (MS)`（亚稳态）组装类型。序列以占位符 `G` 开头后接三肽（如 `GAAC` 表示三肽 `AAC`），`G` 不参与模型计算。

## 亮点

- **多模型投票机制**：SVM、弹性网络逻辑回归、随机森林三个模型共同决策，并输出 `consensus_agreement`（如 3/3 表示高置信度，2/3 为低置信度）。
- **特征工程**：使用 AAindex 氨基酸属性经 PCA 压缩，减少维度并提取关键理化特征。
- **易用性**：提供 Google Colab 一键运行、命令行接口、Python API 和 Jupyter Notebook 多种使用方式。
- **可训练性**：支持用户用自定义数据（CSV 格式，`sequence,label`）训练新模型，并提供了完整的训练流水线（步骤 01–07），包括特征构建、超参数搜索（支持本地并行和 SLURM）、评估、消融实验和最终模型导出。
- **性能报告**：在 64 条标记序列上进行了 4 折 × 20 次重复交叉验证，SVM 达到 Macro-F1 0.536、平衡准确率 0.562、准确率 0.773。

## 为何对本课题有用

本课题关注 IDR/无序蛋白及其相分离与生物分子凝聚体。该仓库直接预测三肽能否形成 `droplet`（液滴）组装，而液滴是相分离形成的生物分子凝聚体的典型形态。虽然它聚焦于三肽（而非完整 IDR），但三肽是 IDR 的最小组成单元，其组装倾向的预测可为理解 IDR 驱动相分离的序列特征提供线索。此外，该工具基于 AAindex 理化性质建模，与 IDR 预测中常用的序列-性质关联方法一致，可作为 IDR 介导凝聚体形成研究的辅助工具。

## 怎么用

**安装**：
```bash
git clone https://github.com/harshavcsn/Lipidation_Classifier_Predictor.git
cd Lipidation_Classifier_Predictor
pip install -r requirements.txt  # 仅预测
pip install -r requirements-train.txt  # 训练模型
```

**预测**：
- 命令行：`python predict.py GAAC GKLV GGWV` 或 `python predict.py --input new_predict.csv --output predictions.csv`
- Python API：
```python
from predict import predict
predict(["GAAC", "GKLV"])
```
- 输入文件：每行一个序列，或 CSV 含 `sequence` 列。

**训练自定义模型**：
1. 准备无表头 CSV，两列 `sequence,label`（如 `list3.csv`）。
2. 运行训练流水线：`LIPML_DATA=my_data.csv LIPML_OUT=results_my_run LIPML_MAX_COMBOS=20 ./run_all.sh 8`（设置 `LIPML_MAX_COMBOS=none` 进行完整搜索）。
3. 用新模型预测：`python predict.py GAAC --models-dir results_my_run/final --pca-table results_my_run/features/pca_table.csv`

所有配置在 `config.py` 中，可在 `models.py` 中启用朴素贝叶斯。

# Lipidation Classifier Predictor

[![Open In Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/assets/colab-badge.svg)](https://colab.research.google.com/github/harshavcsn/Lipidation_Classifier_Predictor/blob/main/predict_colab.ipynb)
![Python](https://img.shields.io/badge/python-3.11%2B-blue)
[![License: MIT](https://img.shields.io/badge/License-MIT-green.svg)](LICENSE)

Predicts whether a **tripeptide** forms a `fiber`, `droplet` or `MetaStable (MS)`
assembly. Each residue is described by AAindex properties compressed with PCA,
and three models (SVM, elastic-net logistic regression, random forest) vote on
the final class.

Sequences are written with a leading `G` placeholder followed by the
tripeptide, e.g. `GAAC` for the tripeptide `AAC`. The `G` is not used by the
models.

---

## Installation

Requires Python 3.11+.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/harshavcsn/Lipidation_Classifier_Predictor.git
cd Lipidation_Classifier_Predictor
pip install -r requirements.txt          # prediction only
pip install -r requirements-train.txt    # also needed to train your own model
```

---

## Predict

**Google Colab (no installation):** click **Open in Colab** above and run all cells.

**Command line:**

```bash
python predict.py GAAC GKLV GGWV
python predict.py --input new_predict.csv --output predictions.csv
```

```
sequence SVM_RBF_pred ElasticNetLogistic_pred RandomForest_pred consensus_pred consensus_agreement
    GAAC        fiber                   fiber             fiber          fiber                 3/3
    GKLV      droplet                 droplet           droplet        droplet                 3/3
    GGWV      droplet                 droplet           droplet        droplet                 3/3
```

`consensus_agreement` shows how many models agree. Treat `2/3` as a
low-confidence call.

**Notebook:** open [`predict.ipynb`](predict.ipynb) in Jupyter or VS Code.

**Python:**

```python
from predict import predict
predict(["GAAC", "GKLV"])
```

Input files can list one sequence per line, or be a CSV with a `sequence` column.

---

## Model performance

Cross-validated on 64 labeled sequences (4-fold × 20 repeats).

| Model | Macro-F1 | Balanced accuracy | Accuracy |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SVM (RBF kernel)** | **0.536** | **0.562** | **0.773** |
| Elastic-net logistic regression | 0.506 | 0.532 | 0.733 |
| Random forest | 0.506 | 0.527 | 0.724 |

---

## Train your own model

1. Prepare a CSV with **no header** and two columns, `sequence,label`, like
   [`list3.csv`](list3.csv).
2. Run the pipeline. This quick run tests 20 settings per model on 8 CPUs; set
   `LIPML_MAX_COMBOS=none` for the full search.

   ```bash
   LIPML_DATA=my_data.csv LIPML_OUT=results_my_run LIPML_MAX_COMBOS=20 ./run_all.sh 8
   ```

3. Predict with your new models:

   ```bash
   python predict.py GAAC --models-dir results_my_run/final \
                          --pca-table results_my_run/features/pca_table.csv
   ```

All settings are in [`config.py`](config.py). Naive Bayes can be switched on
in [`models.py`](models.py).

---

## Files

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `predict.py` | Predict sequences with the trained models |
| `predict.ipynb`, `predict_colab.ipynb` | Prediction notebooks (Jupyter / VS Code, Google Colab) |
| `list3.csv` | Labeled training data |
| `new_predict.csv` | Example sequences to predict |
| `run_all.sh` | Runs the full training pipeline (steps 01–06) |
| `01_build_features.py` | Builds AAindex PCA features |
| `02_make_jobs.py` | Lists every hyperparameter combination to test |
| `run_search.sh`, `run_search.slurm`, `run_shard.py` | Runs the search in parallel (local or SLURM) |
| `03_aggregate.py` | Collects search results and picks the best settings |
| `04_evaluate_best.py` | Confusion matrices and per-class reports |
| `05_ablation.py` | Feature importance and feature-block ablation |
| `06_final_train_predict.py` | Trains the final models on all data |
| `07_export_for_origin.py` | Optional: exports figure data for Origin |
| `config.py`, `features.py`, `models.py`, `cv.py` | Settings and shared code |
| `results_4block_pca/` | Trained models, results and figures from this study |

## 是什么

该仓库是论文 *Interface-mediated secondary phase separation* 的官方代码与数据仓库，提供复现论文中所有数值结果和图表的 MATLAB 代码。其核心是一个三元相场模型（scaffold、client、solvent），用于研究界面介导的次级相分离现象。代码按论文图表组织，每个图表文件夹包含对应的 MATLAB 脚本、预计算的数值数据（.mat）以及必要的辅助函数。

## 亮点

- **完整复现性**：所有图表（主文和补充材料）的生成脚本和数值数据均包含在内，可直接运行复现。
- **多种数值方法**：实现了 Cahn–Hilliard 动力学模拟、径向对称边界值问题（BVP）求解平衡浓度分布、延续计算（continuation）确定失稳边界和临界轮廓，以及界面富集和液滴形态分析。
- **模块化组织**：代码按图表编号（Fig1、Fig2 等）组织，每个图表文件夹内包含独立的脚本和数据，便于定位和复用。
- **参数扫描支持**：部分图表（如 Fig3a、Fig4a）包含参数扫描脚本（run_parameter_scan.m），可系统探索模型参数空间。

## 为何对本课题有用

本课题关注 IDR/无序蛋白的相分离与生物分子凝聚体建模。该仓库提供的三元相场模型和 Cahn–Hilliard 动力学模拟，正是研究相分离动力学和凝聚体形态的经典方法。虽然 README 未明确提及 IDR/无序蛋白，但相分离的物理机制（如 scaffold-client 相互作用、界面富集）与 IDR 介导的凝聚体形成高度相关。该代码可作为相分离建模的参考实现，用于模拟多组分凝聚体的形成、稳定性和形态演化，尤其适合研究界面效应在次级相分离中的作用。

## 怎么用

- **环境要求**：MATLAB，部分脚本需要 Image Processing Toolbox；BVP 计算使用内置的 `bvp4c` 求解器。
- **复现图表**：进入对应图表文件夹（如 `Fig2/Fig2a`），运行其中的 `plot_Fig*.m` 脚本即可生成图表，脚本会读取预计算的 `.mat` 数据。
- **重新生成数据**：如需重新计算数值数据，可运行各图表文件夹中的 `run_dynamics.m`、`run_parameter_scan.m` 或 `compute_critical_profiles.m` 等脚本，它们会调用 `ccode` 子文件夹中的核心函数（如 `get_steady_droplet.m`、`get_steady_ternary.m`、`prepare_fft.m`）。
- **自定义修改**：可基于 `ccode` 中的核心函数修改模型参数（如相互作用强度、组分比例），以探索不同条件下的相分离行为。

# Code for *Interface-mediated secondary phase separation*

This repository contains the MATLAB code and numerical data associated with the manuscript:

**Interface-mediated secondary phase separation**

The code is provided to reproduce the numerical results and figures presented in the main text and Supplementary Information.

## Overview

The numerical calculations are based on a ternary phase-field model describing a scaffold, a client, and a solvent. The repository includes codes for equilibrium calculations, Cahn–Hilliard dynamics, phase-boundary analysis, and generation of the figures presented in the manuscript.

The code is organized primarily by figure. Each figure folder contains the scripts and data required to reproduce the corresponding figure. Additional subfolders are provided when intermediate numerical calculations are required to generate the plotting data.

## Repository Structure

The repository contains folders corresponding to figures in the main text and Supplementary Information.

In general, each figure folder contains:

- MATLAB scripts (`.m`) used to reproduce the figure.
- Precomputed numerical data (`.mat`) used by the plotting scripts.
- Supporting MATLAB functions when required.
- Additional numerical scripts for regenerating the precomputed data when applicable.

## Numerical Methods

The repository includes implementations of:

- Cahn–Hilliard simulations for the dynamics of the ternary mixture.
- Radially symmetric boundary-value problem (BVP) calculations for equilibrium concentration profiles.
- Continuation calculations for determining instability boundaries and critical profiles.
- Analysis of interfacial enrichment and droplet morphology.

## Requirements

The code was developed and tested in MATLAB.

Some scripts may require MATLAB toolboxes, including:

- Image Processing Toolbox

Numerical BVP calculations use MATLAB's `bvp4c` solver.

## Data and Code Availability

All MATLAB scripts and numerical data required to reproduce the computational results presented in the manuscript are included in this repository.
